gold_efu.claim: Nafion 117 in VRFB achieves coulombic efficiency of 96.0% at 40 mA/cm2 and 25 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 25 C, the CE increased monotonically from 96.0% at 40 mA/cm2 to 98.2% at 200 mA/cm2.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 117 in VRFB achieves coulombic efficiency of 98.2% at 200 mA/cm2 and 25 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 25 C, the CE increased monotonically from 96.0% at 40 mA/cm2 to 98.2% at 200 mA/cm2.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 117 in VRFB exhibits voltage efficiency declining from 85.8% at 40 mA/cm2 to 80.2% at 200 mA/cm2 at 25 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: Voltage efficiency exhibited an inverse relationship with current density, declining from 85.8% at 40 mA/cm2 to 80.2% at 200 mA/cm2 at 25 C.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 117 in VRFB achieves energy efficiency of 80.9% at 100 mA/cm2 and 25 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 25 C, the EE decreased gradually from 82.4% at 40 mA/cm2 to 80.9% at 100 mA/cm2, then declined more steeply to 78.7% at 200 mA/cm2.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 117 in VRFB achieves energy efficiency of 83.5% at 40 mA/cm2 and 40 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: The EE at 40 C was 83.5% at 40 mA/cm2, 82.1% at 80 mA/cm2, 81.4% at 100 mA/cm2, 80.6% at 120 mA/cm2, and 79.1% at 200 mA/cm2.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 212 in VRFB achieves coulombic efficiency of 92.1% at 40 mA/cm2 and 25 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 25 C, the CE ranged from 92.1% at 40 mA/cm2 to 95.3% at 200 mA/cm2.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 212 in VRFB achieves voltage efficiency of 86.2% at 100 mA/cm2 and 25 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 100 mA/cm2 and 25 C, Nafion 117 achieved CE of 97.1%, VE of 82.6%, and EE of 80.2%, while Nafion 212 achieved CE of 93.8%, VE of 86.2%, and EE of 80.9%.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 212 in VRFB achieves energy efficiency of 83.8% at 80 mA/cm2 and 40 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 40 C, the Nafion 212 cell achieved EE values of 82.4% at 40 mA/cm2, 83.8% at 80 mA/cm2, 83.2% at 100 mA/cm2, 82.6% at 120 mA/cm2, 81.9% at 160 mA/cm2, and 80.9% at 200 mA/cm2.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 117 has area-specific resistance of 1.65 ohm cm2 at 25 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: Nafion 117 exhibited an area-specific resistance of 1.65 ohm cm2 at 25 C, substantially higher than the 0.85 ohm cm2 measured for Nafion 212 under identical conditions.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 3.2 Temperature Dependence of Area Resistance
gold_efu.claim: Nafion 117 area resistance decreases to 1.32 ohm cm2 at 40 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 40 C, the area resistance of Nafion 117 decreased to 1.32 ohm cm2, while that of Nafion 212 decreased to 0.68 ohm cm2.

gold_efu.claim: At 100 mA/cm2 and 25 C, Nafion 117 CE (97.1%) is higher than Nafion 212 CE (93.8%) by 3.3 percentage points
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 100 mA/cm2 and 25 C, Nafion 117 achieved CE of 97.1%, VE of 82.6%, and EE of 80.2%, while Nafion 212 achieved CE of 93.8%, VE of 86.2%, and EE of 80.9%.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 212 exhibits higher VE than Nafion 117 across all tested conditions, with an advantage of 3-4 percentage points
gold_efu.evidence_text: The lower area-specific resistance of Nafion 212 translated directly into superior voltage efficiency compared to Nafion 117.

gold_efu.claim: At 100 mA/cm2 and 25 C, Nafion 117 and Nafion 212 achieve comparable EE (80.2% vs 80.9%) despite divergent CE/VE composition
gold_efu.evidence_text: Although the EE values were remarkably similar, the underlying composition differed substantially: Nafion 117 prioritized coulombic efficiency at the expense of voltage efficiency, while Nafion 212 achieved the converse balance.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 212 vanadium permeability (3.9 x 10^-7 cm2/s) is approximately 2.2 times higher than Nafion 117 (1.8 x 10^-7 cm2/s)
gold_efu.evidence_text: The vanadium permeability of Nafion 117 was determined to be 1.8 x 10^-7 cm2/s, compared to 3.9 x 10^-7 cm2/s for Nafion 212.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion membranes are produced through copolymerization of tetrafluoroethylene with perfluorinated vinyl ether sulfonyl fluoride followed by hydrolysis to sulfonic acid form
gold_efu.evidence_text: Nafion membranes, produced through copolymerization of tetrafluoroethylene with perfluorinated vinyl ether sulfonyl fluoride followed by hydrolysis to sulfonic acid form, have served as the benchmark material for VRFB research.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 117 possesses equivalent weight of 1100 g/equiv and dry thickness of 183 um
gold_efu.evidence_text: Nafion 117 possesses an equivalent weight of approximately 1100 g/equiv and a dry thickness of 183 um, while Nafion 212 has the same equivalent weight but a substantially reduced thickness of 50.8 um.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 212 has equivalent weight of 1100 g/equiv and dry thickness of 50.8 um
gold_efu.evidence_text: Nafion 117 possesses an equivalent weight of approximately 1100 g/equiv and a dry thickness of 183 um, while Nafion 212 has the same equivalent weight but a substantially reduced thickness of 50.8 um.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion microstructure comprises hydrophilic sulfonic acid clusters embedded within a hydrophobic fluorocarbon backbone
gold_efu.evidence_text: The microphase-separated morphology of Nafion, comprising hydrophilic sulfonic acid clusters embedded within a hydrophobic fluorocarbon backbone, provides excellent proton conductivity and chemical stability.

gold_efu.claim: Vanadium crossover through the membrane creates imbalance in state of charge between positive and negative electrolytes, leading to progressive reduction in accessible discharge capacity
gold_efu.evidence_text: When vanadium ions permeate from one half-cell to the other, they create an imbalance in the state of charge between the positive and negative electrolytes. This imbalance manifests as a progressive reduction in the accessible discharge capacity.

gold_efu.claim: Vanadium crossover-driven self-discharge reactions create local hotspots that accelerate further membrane and electrode degradation
gold_efu.evidence_text: The exothermic nature of these cross-mixing reactions can also create local hotspots within the cell, potentially accelerating further degradation of the membrane and electrode materials.

gold_efu.claim: Estimated capacity fade rate due to vanadium crossover is 0.08% per cycle for Nafion 117 and 0.18% per cycle for Nafion 212 at 100 mA/cm2 and 25 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: The capacity fade rate attributable to vanadium crossover alone is estimated at approximately 0.08% per cycle for Nafion 117 and 0.18% per cycle for Nafion 212 under standard operating conditions at 100 mA/cm2 and 25 C.

gold_efu.claim: CE increases with current density because Faradaic current increases proportionally while crossover flux driven by concentration gradients remains relatively constant
gold_efu.evidence_text: At higher current densities, the Faradaic current increases proportionally while the crossover flux, being driven primarily by concentration gradients, remains relatively constant.

gold_efu.claim: VE decreases with current density due to increasing ohmic polarization and activation polarization, with ohmic overpotential being dominant above 80 mA/cm2
gold_efu.evidence_text: The ohmic overpotential, which is directly proportional to the product of current density and area-specific resistance, increases linearly with current density and constitutes the dominant loss mechanism at current densities above 80 mA/cm2.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 3.2 Temperature Dependence of Area Resistance
gold_efu.claim: Temperature-dependent resistance reduction follows Arrhenius behavior with activation energy of 11.5 kJ/mol, consistent with vehicular proton transport
gold_efu.evidence_text: The activation energy for proton conduction, calculated from the temperature dependence of conductivity, was approximately 11.5 kJ/mol for both membranes, consistent with a vehicular proton transport mechanism.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 5.3 Temperature Effects and Crossover Dynamics
gold_efu.claim: Higher temperature degrades CE through accelerated vanadium crossover as vanadium ion diffusivity increases according to Stokes-Einstein relationship
gold_efu.evidence_text: This reduction reflects the enhanced vanadium crossover at elevated temperature, as the diffusivity of vanadium ions in the membrane increases with temperature according to the Stokes-Einstein relationship.

gold_efu.claim: For long cycle life applications Nafion 117 is preferred due to higher CE and reduced crossover; for power density and cost Nafion 212 is preferred due to lower resistance
gold_efu.evidence_text: For stationary energy storage applications prioritizing long cycle life and minimal maintenance, Nafion 117 offers superior performance due to its higher coulombic efficiency and reduced vanadium crossover.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 212 CE sensitivity to current density is greater than Nafion 117, increasing by 3.2 percentage points compared to 2.2 percentage points over the same range
gold_efu.evidence_text: The sensitivity of CE to current density was more pronounced for Nafion 212 than for Nafion 117, with the CE increasing by 3.2 percentage points over the current density range compared to 2.2 percentage points for Nafion 117.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 5.3 Temperature Effects and Crossover Dynamics
gold_efu.claim: Nafion 212 EE at 40 C exceeds 25 C EE across all current densities, unlike Nafion 117 where the temperature benefit diminishes at higher current densities
gold_efu.evidence_text: Notably, the 40 C EE exceeded the 25 C EE across the entire current density range for Nafion 212, whereas this was not uniformly the case for Nafion 117.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 117 CE at 40 C is approximately 0.3-0.5 percentage points lower than at 25 C across the entire current density range
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 40 C, the CE values were systematically lower than at 25 C by approximately 0.3-0.5 percentage points across the entire current density range.

gold_efu.claim: Nafion 212 achieves VE of 84.8% at 200 mA/cm2 and 40 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 40 C, the Nafion 212 cell achieved VE values of 89.5% at 40 mA/cm2, 87.8% at 80 mA/cm2, 86.9% at 100 mA/cm2, 86.1% at 120 mA/cm2, 85.4% at 160 mA/cm2, and 84.8% at 200 mA/cm2.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 3.1 Ion Exchange Capacity and Water Uptake
gold_efu.claim: SNPBI-1.42 membrane has ion exchange capacity of 1.42 mmol/g and water uptake of 18%
gold_efu.evidence_text: SNPBI-1.42 exhibited the target IEC of 1.42 mmol/g, achieved through controlled post-sulfonation of the parent PBI. The sulfonation process also increased water uptake to 18%, compared to 12% for the acid-doped PBI baseline.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 3.1 Ion Exchange Capacity and Water Uptake
gold_efu.claim: SPTPC-2.59 membrane has ion exchange capacity of 2.59 mmol/g and water uptake of 28%
gold_efu.evidence_text: SPTPC-2.59 exhibited the highest IEC of 2.59 mmol/g among all tested membranes. The water uptake of 28% was correspondingly the highest among the four systems.

gold_efu.claim: SNPBI-1.42 has area-specific resistance of 1.15 ohm cm2
gold_efu.evidence_text: SNPBI-1.42 showed a substantially reduced resistance of 1.15 ohm cm2, demonstrating the effectiveness of covalently bound sulfonic acid groups in providing continuous proton conduction pathways.

gold_efu.claim: SPTPC-2.59 has area-specific resistance of 0.82 ohm cm2, the lowest among all tested non-fluorinated membranes
gold_efu.evidence_text: SPTPC-2.59 achieved the lowest resistance of 0.82 ohm cm2, benefiting from its high IEC and the additional proton conduction contribution from the piperidinium groups.

gold_efu.claim: SNPBI-1.42 has vanadium permeability of 0.95 x 10^-7 cm2/s
gold_efu.evidence_text: SNPBI-1.42 showed a slightly elevated permeability of 0.95 x 10^-7 cm2/s, still substantially lower than commercial Nafion membranes.

gold_efu.claim: SNPBI-1.42 achieves coulombic efficiency of 98.1% at 100 mA/cm2
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 100 mA/cm2, the CE was 98.1%, which is competitive with Nafion 117 and superior to Nafion 212.

gold_efu.claim: SNPBI-1.42 achieves voltage efficiency of 82.1% at 100 mA/cm2
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 100 mA/cm2, the VE was 82.1%.

gold_efu.claim: SNPBI-1.42 achieves energy efficiency of 80.5% at 100 mA/cm2, the highest among all tested non-fluorinated membranes
gold_efu.evidence_text: SNPBI-1.42 demonstrated the highest EE among all tested non-fluorinated membranes. At 100 mA/cm2, the EE was 80.5%, which exceeds the performance of both Nafion 117 and Nafion 212 under comparable conditions.

gold_efu.claim: SPTPC-2.59 achieves energy efficiency of 81.4% at 100 mA/cm2
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 100 mA/cm2, the EE was 81.4%.

gold_efu.claim: PBI achieves coulombic efficiency of 98.2% at 40 mA/cm2, the highest among all tested membranes
gold_efu.evidence_text: PBI achieved the highest CE values among all tested membranes, ranging from 98.2% at 40 mA/cm2 to 98.5% at 200 mA/cm2.

gold_efu.claim: At 100 mA/cm2, SNPBI-1.42 EE (80.5%) exceeds SPEEK/APK EE (77.9%) by 2.6 percentage points
gold_efu.evidence_text: SNPBI-1.42 achieved the highest EE at 80.5% (CE 98.1%, VE 82.1%), followed by SPTPC-2.59 at 81.4% (CE 96.3%, VE 83.8%), then SPEEK/APK at 77.9% (CE 96.8%, VE 80.4%).

gold_efu.claim: SPTPC-2.59 VE (83.8%) exceeds SNPBI-1.42 VE (82.1%) at 100 mA/cm2 due to lower area resistance (0.82 vs 1.15 ohm cm2)
SNPBI-1.42 exhibits the highest selectivity among tested non-fluorinated membranes, combining moderate proton conductivity with low vanadium permeability
gold_efu.evidence_text: SNPBI-1.42 exhibited the highest selectivity among the tested non-fluorinated membranes, combining moderate proton conductivity (low resistance of 1.15 ohm cm2) with low vanadium permeability (0.95 x 10^-7 cm2/s).

gold_efu.claim: Vanadium permeability increases from PBI (0.5 x 10^-7 cm2/s) to SNPBI-1.42 (0.95) to SPEEK/APK (2.1) to SPTPC-2.59 (3.2), showing positive correlation with IEC
gold_efu.evidence_text: PBI exhibited the lowest permeability at 0.5 x 10^-7 cm2/s. SNPBI-1.42 showed 0.95 x 10^-7 cm2/s. SPEEK/APK exhibited 2.1 x 10^-7 cm2/s. SPTPC-2.59 showed 3.2 x 10^-7 cm2/s.

gold_efu.claim: PBI membranes are prepared from polybenzimidazole with inherent viscosity of 0.8-0.9 dL/g and doped with 85% phosphoric acid to achieve 5-6 mole H3PO4 per repeat unit
gold_efu.evidence_text: PBI membranes were prepared by solution casting from 3% PBI (IV = 0.8-0.9 dL/g) in dimethylacetamide. The resulting membranes were doped in 85% phosphoric acid at room temperature for 7 days to achieve acid doping levels of approximately 5-6 mole H3PO4 per PBI repeat unit.

gold_efu.claim: SPEEK/APK blend membranes are prepared at 7:3 weight ratio of SPEEK (IEC 1.8 mmol/g) and APK, yielding effective IEC of 1.26 mmol/g
gold_efu.evidence_text: SPEEK/APK blend membranes were prepared by co-dissolving SPEEK (IEC = 1.8 mmol/g) and APK in N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) at a weight ratio of 7:3. The blend membrane achieved an effective IEC of approximately 1.26 mmol/g.

gold_efu.claim: SPTPC-2.59 is based on a rigid terphenylene backbone with piperidinium functional groups designed for high conductivity and dimensional stability
gold_efu.evidence_text: SPTPC-2.59 represents a high-IEC system based on a rigid terphenylene backbone with piperidinium functional groups, designed to achieve high conductivity while maintaining good dimensional stability.

gold_efu.claim: SNPBI-1.42 is prepared by post-sulfonation of PBI using fuming sulfuric acid with controlled temperature and reaction time
gold_efu.evidence_text: SNPBI-1.42 membranes were prepared by post-sulfonation of PBI using a mixture of fuming sulfuric acid (30% SO3) and concentrated sulfuric acid at controlled temperature and reaction time.

gold_efu.claim: V(V) species attack electron-rich positions on aromatic polymer backbone causing chain scission and loss of mechanical integrity
gold_efu.evidence_text: The primary degradation mechanism involves attack by the strongly oxidizing V(V) species (VO2+) on the aromatic polymer backbone, particularly at electron-rich positions.

gold_efu.claim: Sulfonated polymers undergo desulfonation under strongly acidic and oxidative conditions, progressively reducing IEC and proton conductivity
gold_efu.evidence_text: Sulfonated polymers are additionally susceptible to desulfonation under strongly acidic and oxidative conditions, which progressively reduces IEC and consequently degrades proton conductivity.

gold_efu.claim: SNPBI-1.42 degradation primarily involves gradual desulfonation increasing resistance and reducing VE, while SPTPC-2.59 backbone degradation increases vanadium permeability reducing CE
gold_efu.evidence_text: For SNPBI-1.42, the primary degradation pathway involves gradual desulfonation, which increases resistance and reduces VE over extended cycling. For SPTPC-2.59, backbone degradation may create additional free volume that increases vanadium permeability, leading to declining CE.

gold_efu.claim: Resistance decreases approximately as IEC^-1.8 above the percolation threshold of ~1.0 mmol/g due to formation of interconnected proton transport channels
gold_efu.evidence_text: The resistance decreases approximately as IEC^-1.8 for IEC values above the percolation threshold of approximately 1.0 mmol/g. The transition from isolated hydrophilic clusters to interconnected proton transport channels typically occurs at a critical IEC threshold.

gold_efu.claim: A 0.1 ohm cm2 increase in area resistance decreases EE by 0.4-0.5 percentage points, while a 1.0 x 10^-7 cm2/s increase in vanadium permeability decreases EE by 0.8-1.0 percentage points
gold_efu.evidence_text: The regression coefficients indicate that a 0.1 ohm cm2 increase in area resistance decreases EE by approximately 0.4-0.5 percentage points, while a 1.0 x 10^-7 cm2/s increase in vanadium permeability decreases EE by approximately 0.8-1.0 percentage points.

gold_efu.claim: Vanadium permeability increases by approximately 1.0-1.3 x 10^-7 cm2/s per mmol/g of IEC, as each additional sulfonic acid group proportionally increases hydrophilic domain connectivity
gold_efu.evidence_text: The permeability coefficient increases by approximately 1.0-1.3 x 10^-7 cm2/s per mmol/g of IEC above the baseline set by the non-sulfonated polymer matrix. This linear relationship suggests that each additional sulfonic acid group contributes proportionally to the size and connectivity of hydrophilic domains.

gold_efu.claim: PBI exhibits excellent chemical stability due to electron-deficient benzimidazole ring being less susceptible to electrophilic attack by V(V) species
gold_efu.evidence_text: The PBI backbone exhibits excellent chemical stability due to the electron-deficient nature of the benzimidazole ring, which is less susceptible to electrophilic attack by V(V) species.

gold_efu.claim: SNPBI-1.42 is optimal for maximum energy efficiency applications (EE 80.5% at 100 mA/cm2), SPTPC-2.59 for maximum voltage efficiency, while PBI is limited to low current density due to high resistance
gold_efu.evidence_text: For applications requiring maximum energy efficiency across a range of current densities, SNPBI-1.42 represents the optimal choice among the tested membranes. For applications prioritizing maximum voltage efficiency and power density, SPTPC-2.59 offers advantages. PBI is not recommended for practical VRFB operation at current densities above 60 mA/cm2.

gold_efu.claim: SPEEK/APK has area-specific resistance of 1.38 ohm cm2
gold_efu.evidence_text: SPEEK/APK exhibited an intermediate resistance of 1.38 ohm cm2.

gold_efu.claim: PBI has area-specific resistance of 2.45 ohm cm2, the highest among all tested membranes
gold_efu.evidence_text: PBI exhibited the highest resistance at 2.45 ohm cm2, reflecting the relatively low proton mobility in the acid-doped system at room temperature.

gold_efu.claim: SPTPC-2.59 achieves voltage efficiency of 83.8% at 100 mA/cm2, competitive with Nafion 212
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 100 mA/cm2, the VE was 83.8%, which is competitive with Nafion 212 and superior to Nafion 117.

gold_efu.claim: SPEEK/APK achieves coulombic efficiency of 96.8% at 100 mA/cm2
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 100 mA/cm2, the CE was 96.8%.

gold_efu.claim: The C-C electrode exhibits a contact angle of 130.4 deg indicating strong hydrophobic character
gold_efu.evidence_text: The C-C electrode exhibited a contact angle of 130.4 deg, indicating strong hydrophobic character typical of untreated carbon felts.

gold_efu.claim: The MC-C electrode shows a contact angle of 102 deg after mild acid etching treatment
gold_efu.evidence_text: The MC-C electrode showed a substantially reduced contact angle of 102 deg, demonstrating that mild acid etching effectively introduced oxygen-containing functional groups and increased surface polarity.

gold_efu.claim: The BMC-C electrode achieves a contact angle of 92.8 deg with boron doping and thermal treatment
gold_efu.evidence_text: The BMC-C electrode achieved the lowest contact angle of 92.8 deg, suggesting that boron doping further enhanced the surface hydrophilicity through additional polar sites and modified electronic structure.

gold_efu.claim: The C-C electrode has a charge-transfer resistance of 3.82 ohm cm2
gold_efu.evidence_text: The C-C electrode presented the highest Rct value of 3.82 ohm cm2, reflecting the inherently poor electrocatalytic activity of untreated carbon surfaces toward vanadium redox reactions.

gold_efu.claim: The MC-C electrode demonstrates a charge-transfer resistance of 2.17 ohm cm2 after mild acid etching
gold_efu.evidence_text: The MC-C electrode demonstrated a substantially reduced Rct of 2.17 ohm cm2, representing a 43.2% decrease relative to C-C.

gold_efu.claim: The BMC-C electrode achieves a charge-transfer resistance of 1.34 ohm cm2 with boron doping
gold_efu.evidence_text: The BMC-C electrode achieved the lowest Rct of 1.34 ohm cm2, corresponding to a 64.9% reduction compared to C-C and a 38.2% reduction compared to MC-C.

gold_efu.claim: At 100 mA/cm2, the C-C electrode achieves a coulombic efficiency of 94%, the MC-C electrode attains 96%, and the BMC-C electrode reaches 97%
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 100 mA/cm2, the C-C electrode achieved a CE of 94%, while the MC-C electrode attained 96%, and the BMC-C electrode reached 97%.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 3.4 Voltage Efficiency and Energy Efficiency
gold_efu.claim: At 100 mA/cm2, C-C electrode shows VE of 70%, MC-C shows 77%, and BMC-C shows 85%
gold_efu.evidence_text: The C-C electrode exhibited a VE of 70%, consistent with the significant overpotential associated with its high charge-transfer resistance. The MC-C electrode demonstrated improved VE of 77%, reflecting the reduced kinetic limitations achieved through surface roughening and oxygen functionalization. The BMC-C electrode achieved the highest VE of 85%.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 3.4 Voltage Efficiency and Energy Efficiency
gold_efu.claim: At 100 mA/cm2, C-C delivers EE of 65.8%, MC-C achieves 73.9%, and BMC-C reaches 82.5%
gold_efu.evidence_text: At 100 mA/cm2, the C-C electrode delivered an EE of 65.8%, calculated from 94% CE and 70% VE. The MC-C electrode achieved an EE of 73.9%, derived from 96% CE and 77% VE. The BMC-C electrode reached an EE of 82.5%, computed from 97% CE and 85% VE.

gold_efu.claim: Surface roughness Ra increases from 8.4 um for C-C to 11.2 um for MC-C to 14.7 um for BMC-C
gold_efu.evidence_text: The C-C electrode displayed a mean roughness Ra of 8.4 um, characteristic of the relatively smooth fiber surfaces of commercial carbon felt. The MC-C electrode exhibited increased roughness with Ra of 11.2 um. The BMC-C electrode showed the highest roughness with Ra of 14.7 um.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 3.4 Voltage Efficiency and Energy Efficiency
gold_efu.claim: BMC-C electrode achieves 16.7 percentage point higher EE than C-C electrode at 100 mA/cm2
gold_efu.evidence_text: The 16.7 percentage point improvement in EE from C-C to BMC-C underscores the practical significance of the progressive modification strategy for enhancing the round-trip energy storage efficiency of VRFB systems.

gold_efu.claim: BMC-C reduces charge-transfer resistance by 64.9% compared to C-C and by 38.2% compared to MC-C
gold_efu.evidence_text: The BMC-C electrode achieved the lowest Rct of 1.34 ohm cm2, corresponding to a 64.9% reduction compared to C-C and a 38.2% reduction compared to MC-C.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 3.5 Performance at Varied Current Densities
gold_efu.claim: Performance gap between modified and unmodified electrodes widens as current density increases from 50 to 500 mA/cm2
gold_efu.evidence_text: As current density increased to 200 mA/cm2, the performance gap between the modified and unmodified electrodes widened, with BMC-C maintaining substantially higher VE and EE values compared to C-C.

gold_efu.claim: The BMC-C electrode contains boron heteroatoms incorporated into the carbon lattice through heat treatment at 750 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: The etched felt was soaked in a boric acid solution (0.3 mol/L) for 2 hours, dried at 80 C, and then heat-treated at 750 C under argon atmosphere for 2 hours to incorporate boron heteroatoms into the carbon lattice.

gold_efu.claim: MC-C electrode surface contains oxygen-containing functional groups introduced by HNO3 etching at 80 C
gold_efu.evidence_text: The MC-C electrode was prepared by immersing the commercial carbon felt in a 5.0 mol/L HNO3 solution at 80 C for 6 hours, followed by thorough washing with deionized water and drying at 120 C overnight.

gold_efu.claim: C-C electrode exhibits gradual performance degradation over 200 cycles through progressive oxidation and loss of active surface area
gold_efu.evidence_text: The C-C electrode exhibited gradual performance degradation characterized by increasing overpotential and declining VE over 200 cycles. This degradation pattern is consistent with the progressive oxidation and loss of limited active surface area on untreated carbon felt.

gold_efu.claim: MC-C electrode shows performance decline after extended cycling due to gradual leaching of oxygen functional groups under acidic and oxidizing conditions
gold_efu.evidence_text: The MC-C electrode showed improved stability compared to C-C, though some performance decline was observed after extended cycling, potentially associated with the gradual leaching or reduction of oxygen functional groups under the strongly acidic and oxidizing environment of the positive half-cell.

gold_efu.claim: Vanadium crossover is influenced by electrode overpotential through local concentration polarization effects
gold_efu.evidence_text: The reduced overpotential on BMC-C decreases the extent of concentration polarization during charge, which modestly reduces the driving force for vanadium ion crossover from the positive to negative half-cell.

gold_efu.claim: The correlation between surface roughness and electrochemical performance suggests increased triple-phase boundaries facilitate redox reactions
gold_efu.evidence_text: The correlation between surface roughness and electrochemical performance suggests that the increased Ra from 8.4 um to 14.7 um creates additional triple-phase boundaries where the electrode, electrolyte, and reactant species meet.

gold_efu.claim: Boron doping modifies electronic structure to lower activation energy for electron transfer between electrode and vanadium species
gold_efu.evidence_text: Boron doping modifies the electronic structure to lower the activation energy for electron transfer between the electrode and vanadium species.

gold_efu.claim: MC-C offers favorable cost-performance balance with 73.9% EE while BMC-C provides maximum performance at 82.5% EE for high-efficiency applications
gold_efu.evidence_text: For cost-sensitive applications, the MC-C treatment offers a favorable balance between performance improvement and processing cost, achieving a 73.9% EE at 100 mA/cm2 with a relatively simple acid etching procedure. For high-efficiency applications, the BMC-C electrode provides state-of-the-art performance with 82.5% EE at 100 mA/cm2, though the additional boron doping and thermal treatment steps increase manufacturing complexity.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 3.3 Effect of Flow Rate on Mass Transfer and Efficiency
gold_efu.claim: Pumping power increases from 5 mW at 10 mL/min to 50 mW at 100 mL/min flow rate
gold_efu.evidence_text: The measured pumping power increased from approximately 5 mW at 10 mL/min to 50 mW at 100 mL/min, following a non-linear relationship with flow rate that reflected both viscous losses and pump efficiency characteristics.

gold_efu.source_section: Section 3.4 Gross and Net Energy Efficiency Analysis
gold_efu.claim: Gross energy efficiency ranges from 78% to 87% across all tested conditions
gold_efu.evidence_text: Gross EE values ranged from 78% to 87%, with the highest values achieved at moderate vanadium concentrations (1.6 mol/L), optimal H2SO4 concentration (3.0 mol/L), moderate to high flow rates (40-100 mL/min), and lower current densities (50 mA/cm2).
